chunks: 2313 - It has been narrated from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, who said:
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام said to us: “Which of the places is most virtuous?” So we said: “Allah, His Messenger, and the son of His Messenger know best.”

He said: “As for the most virtuous of places, it is what is between the Rukn and the Maqām. And if a man were given the lifespan that Nūḥ عليه السلام lived among his people—one thousand years except fifty years—fasting by day and standing in prayer by night in that place, then he met Allah, Mighty and Majestic, without our wilayah, that would not benefit him in any way.”

key_terms.لَمْ يَنْفَعْهُ ذَلِكَ شَيْئًا: that would not benefit him in any way
key_terms.وَلَايَتِنَا: our wilayah; allegiance and divinely ordained authority of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.يَقُومُ اللَّيْلَ: he stands in prayer during the night

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the most virtuous place in the Kaʿbah and the importance of wilayah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the area between the Rukn and the Maqām is the most virtuous of places. It also teaches that even the greatest acts of worship in the holiest place do not benefit a person without the wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
